title: Kansas City Ribs
subtitle: Pork spare ribs with a thick, sweet-and-sticky tomato glaze
excerpt: Kansas City ribs are spare ribs coated in a thick, sweet tomato-based sauce that caramelises in the oven to a sticky, dark finish. They're the most widely recognised American rib style: rich, sweet, with a gently spiced rub underneath the sauce.
sourceNotes: Kansas City-style barbecue ribs are characterised by their sweet, thick tomato-molasses sauce applied heavily and caramelised to a lacquer. The style developed in Kansas City restaurants in the early 20th century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooked ribs in foil. Reheat at 180°C covered for 20 minutes, then brush with extra sauce and uncover for 10 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook through the covered phase a day ahead and refrigerate. Finish with the sauce for 30 minutes at 200°C.

content.text: Kansas City ribs are the sweet end of the American rib spectrum: spare ribs rubbed with spices, cooked slowly until tender, then finished under a thick, sticky tomato-and-molasses sauce that caramelises to a dark lacquer. The sauce is applied in coats over the final 30 minutes of cooking, each layer building on the last. The result is deeply sweet, slightly smoky, and rich enough to require napkins.

Heat the oven to 150°C (fan 130°C / gas mark 2). Remove the membrane from the bone side of the {{pork-ribs}}. Mix together {{paprika-smoked}}, {{dark-brown-sugar}}, {{garlic-powder}}, {{onion-powder}}, {{sea-salt-flakes}}, and {{black-pepper}}. Pat the rack dry and coat it all over with the rub.
Place meat side up on a foil-lined baking tray. Cover tightly with foil and cook for two and a half hours, until the meat has pulled back from the bone ends.

In a small saucepan, combine {{ketchup}}, {{dark-brown-sugar}}, and {{cider-vinegar}}. Add {{molasses}}, {{worcestershire-sauce}}, {{garlic-powder}}, {{paprika-smoked}}, and {{mustard-powder}}. Heat gently, stirring, for five minutes until smooth and slightly thick. Taste and adjust.
Remove the foil. Increase the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / gas mark 6). Brush a generous coat of sauce over the meat side. Return to the oven uncovered for 10 minutes.

Brush on a second layer and cook for another 10 minutes. Add a third coat and cook for a final 10 minutes. The surface should be dark, sticky, and slightly charred at the edges. Rest ten minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: The sauce burns before it caramelises
items.cause: Too much sugar in the sauce, or oven too hot.
items.fix: Watch the ribs closely during the sauce phase. If the sauce looks like it's burning (black patches spreading from the edges), remove the ribs and let the oven come down to 190°C before continuing.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and runny, not sticky
items.cause: Not reduced enough on the hob.
items.fix: The sauce needs to simmer for at least five minutes before applying. If it's still thin, simmer another two to three minutes. The molasses is what gives it body.

items.symptom: The ribs are underdone and tough after the sauce phase
items.cause: The covered phase was too short.
items.fix: The covered phase is the critical one. The sauce phase is just the finish: if the ribs aren't tender when you remove the foil, cover them again and cook another 30 minutes before starting the sauce.

items.symptom: The sauce has a harsh, bitter edge
items.cause: Molasses can be quite bitter, especially blackstrap.
items.fix: Use regular (not blackstrap) molasses, or substitute black treacle. Add a pinch more sugar to balance.

content.text: Kansas City is the American city most linked to BBQ sauce: thick, sweet, tomato and treacle based, applied generously and caramelised dark. The city draws from several barbecue traditions and made the style its own. KC-style sauce is the default in American supermarkets. The homemade version is better: more complex and less sweet.
